newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BANKS '96 PROFITS GREW BY +10 PCT - BANKER.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BANKS '96 PROFITS GREW BY +10 PCT - BANKER.

text.p: The Belgian banking sector's 1996 profits should grow on average by more than 10 percent due to last year's low interest rates and steep yield curve, Belgian Banking Association chairman Willy Breesch said on Wednesday.
"Profit growth in the sector should be better than in 1995. I think 1996 profits will show growth of more than 10 percent on average," he told Reuters in an interview.
"But that is not a structural growth. Commercial margins remain under pressure. The profit growth is due to the favourable interest rate climate we enjoyed last year," he added.
Breesch said that the low short-term interest rates last year had a triple positive effect on bank earnings:
- there was a strong influx of cheap funding due to the success of the bank savings books (as investors refuse to commit funds to longer-term savings instruments;
- banks made good profits on the transformation of low-yielding short-term deposits into longer-term loans;
- low interest rates made off-balance sheet products such as investment funds more popular, thus boosting banks' fee income.
Breesch said it would be too simplistic to extrapolate last year's trend towards 1997.

Non-listed Paribas Bank Belgium kicked off the banks' earnings season today, announcing a 30 percent jump in group net profit to 3.97 billion francs from 3.06 billion. The rise was mainly due to profit from financial transactions.
Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL) will publish results on March 5, followed by Generale Bank on March 11, Kredietbank on March 13 and CCB on April 2.
Breesch also said that he was cool about Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt's call last year for further mergers in the Belgian banking sector.
"I never understood the motivation for his appeal. I am not saying it is not a good idea. There has been a lot of talk about it, but not much has happened," he said.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
